goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — On a read error, nil is stored in the cache, so in non-Dev every later request misses and re-reads the manifest one at a time behind the exclusive lock held for the whole I/O

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows introducing an RWMutex and taking an exclusive Lock (deferred Unlock) after a cache miss; it does not show any error-handling path or any assignment that would “store nil in the cache on a read error.” Without the later code that sets `entryPointAssetsCache`, the claim about caching nil and causing repeated misses on errors is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Nothing re-checks the cache after taking the write lock, so on a cold start every concurrent index request that missed waits in line and then re-reads and re-parses the manifest itself (serialized thundering herd).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RLock fast-path, then always takes the write lock on a miss, but does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`. If multiple goroutines miss concurrently, the first will populate the cache, yet subsequent goroutines that were waiting will still proceed to recompute/parse rather than returning the now-populated cache. This is a real, diff-grounded inefficiency (serialized duplicate work), but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:69 — Failures are never cached (nil is stored on error), so a missing or bad manifest makes every request take the exclusive lock and redo file I/O and JSON decode one at a time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows adding an RWMutex and taking an exclusive lock before computing `result`, but it does not show the later code that sets `entryPointAssetsCache` on success or error. The claim that “nil is stored on error” and that failures are never cached cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev mode every call skips the cache and holds the global write lock across file open and JSON decode, so all concurrent index renders run one at a time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that if the early return is not taken (notably when cfg.Env == setting.Dev), the function unconditionally acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and defers Unlock(), meaning the rest of GetWebAssets executes under the global write lock. That will serialize concurrent callers in Dev mode. The claim about specific operations (file open/JSON decode) isn’t shown in the snippet, but the lock scope across the entire remainder of the function is verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — The CDN path would do a network fetch with http.DefaultClient (no timeout) while holding the global write lock, so one slow CDN response would block every index render (currently dead code because cdn is hardcoded to "").

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and takes the write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); defer ...Unlock()`) for the remainder of `GetWebAssets` whenever the cache is empty or in dev mode. That means any potentially slow work done later in the function (not shown in the diff) will now run while holding the global write lock, blocking concurrent callers. However, the finding’s specific details about a CDN network fetch via `http.DefaultClient` and the CDN being hardcoded to "" are not verifiable from the provided diff snippet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — After acquiring the write lock the cache is not re-checked, so concurrent cold-start (or post-failure) callers serialize and each redundantly re-read/re-parse the manifest (thundering herd behind one lock).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and does an initial RLock read of `entryPointAssetsCache`, but after falling through it takes a write `Lock()` without re-checking whether another goroutine populated `entryPointAssetsCache` while this one was waiting. From the shown code, multiple concurrent callers seeing `ret == nil` will each proceed under the write lock and redundantly rebuild the assets instead of using the now-populated cache. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/efficiency issue (not a correctness break) consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — Exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromCDN, which uses http.DefaultClient with no timeout; if the CDN path is enabled, a slow/hung fetch blocks every page request waiting on the lock (latent today since cdn is hardcoded "").

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and now takes an exclusive Lock with `defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()` immediately after a cache miss, meaning the lock is held for the remainder of `GetWebAssets` while it computes/fetches `result`. That creates a real contention risk if the rest of the function performs slow work (e.g., network/disk reads) because all concurrent callers will block on the lock. However, the specific claim about `readWebAssetsFromCDN` using `http.DefaultClient` with no timeout is not shown in this diff, so that part can’t be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:56 — A single request's ctx is used to populate a process-wide cache, so one client cancellation/transient CDN error triggers the file fallback and that result is cached permanently in non-dev mode with no retry of the CDN (latent while cdn is "").

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds an RWMutex around the existing global `entryPointAssetsCache` and changes the early-return to read via the mutex. It does not show how `ctx` is used to fetch assets, any CDN/file fallback logic, or that a cancellation/error result is cached permanently. Those behaviors are not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — sync.RWMutex.Lock is not context-aware, so waiting callers cannot abandon on request cancellation/deadline while another goroutine holds the lock.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a package-level RWMutex and uses `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`/`RLock()` inside `GetWebAssets(ctx, ...)`. Go’s `sync.RWMutex` indeed can block indefinitely regardless of `ctx` cancellation/deadline, so callers can’t stop waiting on the lock. However, this is a general concurrency/architecture concern (potentially increasing latency under contention) rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff, since the diff doesn’t show any required context-aware locking behavior or an actual deadlock/leak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In Dev env every call takes the exclusive write lock and re-reads the manifest, serializing all concurrent index page loads (previously unserialized).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and, after the initial RLock/RUnlock and early-return check, unconditionally takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with a deferred Unlock(). Since the early return only triggers when cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil, the Dev environment path will always acquire the exclusive write lock for the remainder of GetWebAssets. This necessarily serializes concurrent calls in Dev, whereas previously Dev calls would not contend on this new lock at all (no mutex existed). This is a real, diff-grounded concurrency/performance concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:40 — Concurrency fix ships with no test at all (no webassets_test.go, no callers with tests); no concurrent `go test -race` test of GetWebAssets proves the data race is actually fixed or guards against regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial concurrency logic (global `entryPointAssetsCache` now guarded by `sync.RWMutex` with `RLock`/`Lock` in `GetWebAssets`), but the PR diff shown does not add any tests to validate concurrent access or prevent regression (e.g., a race-focused test exercising parallel `GetWebAssets` calls). The finding’s broader claim that there are no existing tests anywhere can’t be proven from this diff, but it is grounded that this change itself ships without new test coverage.
